mcqs.question: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a concave mirror whose focal length is 15 cm. Using the mirror formula and the Cartesian sign convention, what is the image distance?
mcqs.explanation: For a concave mirror, f = -15 cm and object distance u = -30 cm (real object in front). Mirror formula: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u → 1/v = 1/f – 1/u = -1/15 - (-1/30) = -1/30, so v = -30 cm. The negative sign indicates a real image on the same side as the object.

mcqs.question: A convex mirror has a focal length of +20 cm. An object is placed 40 cm in front of the mirror. According to the Cartesian sign convention, what is the image distance?
mcqs.explanation: For a convex mirror, f = +20 cm and u = -40 cm. Mirror formula: 1/v = 1/f – 1/u = 1/20 - (-1/40) = 1/20 + 1/40 = 3/40, so v = 40/3 ≈ +13.33 cm. Positive v denotes a virtual image behind the mirror.

mcqs.question: A concave mirror has a focal length of -10 cm. An object is placed exactly at the focal point (10 cm from the mirror). Many think the image forms at the focal point; what is the correct image position?

options.C: 5 cm in front of the mirror
options.D: 10 cm in front of the mirror

mcqs.explanation: When the object is at the focal point of a concave mirror (u = -f), the mirror formula gives 1/v = 1/f – 1/u = -1/10 - (-1/10) = 0, so v → ∞. The image forms at infinity, not at the focal point.

mcqs.question: For a concave mirror with focal length -15 cm, an object is placed 30 cm in front of the mirror. What is the magnification of the image?
mcqs.explanation: Using the mirror formula, u = -30 cm, f = -15 cm gives v = -30 cm. Magnification m = -v/u = -(-30)/(-30) = -1. The magnitude 1 means the image is the same size as the object, and the negative sign indicates it is inverted.

mcqs.question: A concave mirror produces an image with magnification -2, while a convex mirror produces an image with magnification +0.5. Which statement correctly describes the nature of both images?

options.B: The concave image is real and inverted; the convex image is virtual and upright
options.C: Both images are real and upright
options.D: The concave image is virtual and upright; the convex image is real and inverted

mcqs.answer: The concave image is real and inverted; the convex image is virtual and upright
mcqs.explanation: Negative magnification (-2) for the concave mirror indicates a real, inverted image that is twice the size of the object. Positive magnification (+0.5) for the convex mirror indicates a virtual, upright image that is half the size of the object.

mcqs.question: A concave mirror of focal length -12 cm forms a real image that is twice the size of the object. Find the object distance.
mcqs.explanation: For a real, inverted image twice the size, magnification m = -2. Using m = -v/u → v = 2u. Mirror formula: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u = 1/(2u) + 1/u = 3/(2u). Hence u = 3f/2 = 3(-12)/2 = -18 cm. The negative sign shows the object is in front of the mirror.

mcqs.question: Which of the following equations correctly represents the mirror formula for spherical mirrors?
mcqs.explanation: The standard mirror formula relating focal length (f), object distance (u) and image distance (v) is 1/f = 1/v + 1/u, where sign conventions are applied as per the Cartesian system.

mcqs.question: According to the Cartesian sign convention for mirrors, the object distance is taken as:

options.D: Depends on the type of mirror

mcqs.explanation: In the Cartesian sign convention, distances measured against the direction of incident light (i.e., in front of the mirror where a real object is placed) are taken as negative. Hence object distance is negative.
